messages.content: You are analyzing historical measurements for avGFP fluorescence. Larger log brightness is better. Only observations have measured fluorescence. Menu values and tool scores are fitted predictions. Use the observed evidence, state a testable short hypothesis, and specify edits that match displayed candidate identities on the pinned GFP reference. The reference menu is optional. The scoring tool can construct and score legal off-menu edits. Do not estimate or cite measurements for candidates. Keep all text fields concise and evidence-specific.

Call score_gfp_designs immediately with a short analyst summary, a short hypothesis, 1–3 observed O aliases and exactly 6 designs. Write each design as a C alias followed by its exact edits, or NEW followed by a space and 1–4 colon-separated substitutions. Include at least one NEW design. Exclude observed IDs and pending_ids from NEW. The tool assigns N aliases to valid off-menu edits. Give one short design_reasons entry per design in the same order, starting with a displayed O alias and a space. Each reason must be under 15 words. State a testable fluorescence hypothesis. Predeclare target_design as its 1-based design index and target_reference as one of your cited measured O aliases. The primary design predicts its measured fluorescence will strictly exceed that observation. When using the menu as a measured comparison, nominate a menu design that tests the hypothesis. The primary design must be in your final batch. In feedback_adjustment, state a concrete decision change based on the available test result, or note the available evidence if no test has returned. Keep all explanations brief. arguments.feedback_adjustment: Round-1 forecast was supported (O6 measured 3.562, above O4), so I raise weight on conservative charge/repacking designs and now test C02 against O4 instead of a buried-polar combination.
